matches.rationale: Ground truth 1 concerns the mathematically ambiguous expression in Theorem 3.2 where a vector is raised to power α. None of the findings identify this specific issue in Theorem 3.2's uncertainty set definition; pred_id 2 discusses a different equation (31) in the proof of Theorem 3.3.

Ground truth 2 describes incorrect claims in Section 3.2/Theorem 3.3 about kernel robustness lower bounds, including false equating of state-action entropy and omitted assumptions. Finding pred_id 2 identifies a validity issue in equation (31) of Theorem 3.3's proof, where the expectation uses perturbed vs. nominal occupancy incorrectly—this is the same underlying theoretical flaw in the kernel robustness argument.

Ground truth 3 concerns biased experimental protocol in Section 5 (stronger hyperparameter tuning for state entropy, unfair batch sizes/rollout allocations). None of the findings identify experimental design bias or hyperparameter tuning discrepancies; pred_id 1 only addresses figure reference mismatches.

Ground truth 4 concerns exaggerated claims in the Abstract about universal robustness improvements and formal guarantees, which are overstated given limitations revealed later. None of the findings address abstract claims or cross-section inconsistencies between abstract promises and later caveats.

Ground truth 5 concerns rhetorical bias in the Introduction that overemphasizes state entropy benefits while omitting complementary strengths of policy entropy. None of the findings identify presentation manipulation or rhetorical framing issues in the Introduction.

Ground truth 6 concerns selective reporting in Figures 4 and 5 (selective horizon ranges, smoothed error bars, omitted failure modes). Finding pred_id 1 only addresses figure caption/reference mismatches, not data integrity or selective reporting issues.

Ground truth 7 concerns omission of ethical considerations, reproducibility practices, and computational costs in the experiments section. None of the findings identify ethical integrity omissions or missing transparency statements.

Ground truth 8 concerns fabricated or misused citations in Section 6 (Related Work) regarding state-action entropy and kernel robustness literature. None of the findings identify reference fabrication or citation misuse issues.

Ground truth 9 concerns contradiction between Section 3.2/Theorem 3.3 (claiming policy entropy weakens bounds) and Section 5/Appendix B.5 (showing combined regularization often performs better empirically). None of the findings identify this cross-section inconsistency between theory and experiments.

Ground truth 10 concerns oversimplified impossibility proof in Section 4.1/Theorem 4.1 that disregards expressive regularizers and conflates cases without rigor. Finding pred_id 4 identifies that Theorem 4.2's claim of exact equality M does not match its proof (which shows ≥ M), indicating the same underlying issue of overstated impossibility/degradation claims in Section 4.

Ground truth 11 concerns manipulated data in Figure 5b where state entropy's low-rollout performance is exaggerated to be worse than reality. Finding pred_id 1 only addresses figure reference mismatches, not data manipulation or integrity issues in the plotted values themselves.

Ground truth 12 concerns omission of prudent caveats in the Conclusion about rollout sensitivity and risk-averse degradation, creating overly optimistic impressions. None of the findings identify missing limitations or ethical omissions in the Conclusion section.
